content: 1. Cases of liver failure, including those resulting in liver transplantation or death, have been reported with the use of terbinafine tablets. These cases have occurred in individuals both with and without pre-existing liver disease. 2. Most reported liver cases associated with terbinafine use involved patients with serious underlying systemic conditions. 3. The severity of hepatic events and their outcomes may be worse in patients with active or chronic liver disease. 4. Terbinafine treatment should be discontinued if there is biochemical or clinical evidence of liver injury. 5. Terbinafine tablets are not recommended for patients with chronic or active liver disease. 6. Liver function tests should be performed prior to prescribing terbinafine tablets, as hepatotoxicity can occur in patients with or without pre-existing liver disease. 7. Periodic monitoring of liver function tests is recommended during treatment. 8. Terbinafine hydrochloride should be immediately discontinued if liver function tests show elevated levels. 9. Patients prescribed terbinafine tablets should be instructed to promptly report symptoms such as persistent nausea, anorexia, fatigue, vomiting, right upper abdominal pain, jaundice, dark urine, or pale stools to their physician. 10. Patients experiencing these symptoms should stop taking oral terbinafine, and their liver function should be evaluated immediately. 11. Taste disturbances, including loss of taste, have been reported with terbinafine use. 12. These disturbances can be severe enough to cause reduced food intake, weight loss, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. 13. Taste disturbances may resolve within several weeks after discontinuation of treatment, but in some cases, they may persist for more than a year or become permanent. 14. If taste disturbance symptoms occur, terbinafine tablets should be discontinued. 15. Smell disturbances, including loss of smell, have been reported with terbinafine use. 16. Smell disturbances may resolve after stopping treatment, but they can also persist for more than a year or become permanent. 17. If symptoms of smell disturbance occur, terbinafine tablets should be discontinued. 18. Depressive symptoms have been reported during post-marketing use of terbinafine tablets. 19. Prescribers should remain vigilant for the development of depressive symptoms, and patients should be instructed to report such symptoms to their physician. 20. Transient decreases in absolute lymphocyte counts (ALCs) have been observed in controlled clinical trials. 21. Approximately 2% of patients experienced ALC reductions below 1000/mm³ on two or more occasions. 22. In patients with known or suspected immunodeficiency, physicians should consider monitoring complete blood counts if treatment continues for more than six weeks. 23. Cases of severe neutropenia have been reported, which were reversible upon discontinuation of terbinafine tablets, with or without supportive therapy. 24. If clinical signs or symptoms suggestive of secondary infection occur, a complete blood count should be obtained. 25. If the neutrophil count is ≤1000 cells/mm³, terbinafine tablets should be discontinued, and supportive management should be initiated. 26. Serious skin and hypersensitivity reactions have been reported post-marketing. 27. Manifestations of Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) syndrome may include skin reactions (e.g., rash or exfoliative dermatitis), eosinophilia, and organ complications such as hepatitis, pneumonitis, nephritis, myocarditis, or pericarditis. 28. If progressive skin rash or signs/symptoms of the above drug reactions occur, terbinafine treatment should be discontinued. 29. Cases of precipitation and exacerbation of cutaneous and systemic lupus erythematosus have been reported during post-marketing use of terbinafine tablets. 30. Terbinafine tablets should be discontinued in patients with clinical signs and symptoms suggestive of lupus erythematosus. 31. Measurement of serum transaminases (ALT and AST) is advised for all patients before initiating terbinafine tablets.
